Department(OPH) Office of Public Health Job Description:ResponsibilitiesHealth Research, Inc. is seeking an Hourly Project Assistant II to assist with accreditation efforts, supporting the Local Health Department (LHD) Accreditation Crosswalk Project. The New York State Department of Health (NYSDOH) is an accredited health department through the Public Health Accreditation Board (PHAB). As the accrediting body for public health in the United States, PHAB advances standards of excellence and accountability for the systems that promote and protect the health of all people. The Hourly Project Assistant II will assist with the review of the State Health Department’s submitted PHAB Required Documentation. This review seeks to identify documents that New York State (NYS) LHDs can utilize for their respective accreditation or reaccreditation. This position is part of the Pathways to Public Health Internship Program and the purpose is to help strengthen career pathways to public health by bringing together students of all disciplines and academic levels with public health professionals to create a space of exploration, learning, and development. This position will last approximately 10 weeks from 9/14/2026 to 11/27/2026. Minimum QualificationsCurrently enrolled in, or have completed, a degree, certificate, or training program in a related field. Preferred QualificationsExperience using Microsoft Office applications (e.g., Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook) to prepare documents, organize information, analyze data, or develop presentations.Demonstrated analytical or problem‑solving experience through academic projects, research activities, data analysis, or work assignmentsExperience supporting or coordinating projects, such as tracking tasks, organizing materials, meeting deadlines, or assisting with project deliverablesExperience producing written or oral communications, including reports, presentations, emails, or class assignmentsDemonstrated attention to detail evidenced by work involving data entry, documentation, quality review, research, or administrative tasksExperience delivering presentationsExperience or exposure to compliance‑related activities, public health programs, accreditation processes, audits, or regulatory environments Conditions of EmploymentHourly, grant funded position expected to last through 11/27/2026. Compliance with funding requirements such as time and effort reporting, grant deliverables, and contract deliverables, is required. Valid and unrestricted authorization to work in the U.S. is required. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position. Travel up to 10% of the time will be required. The selected candidate must reside within a reasonable commuting distance of the official work location specified in the job posting and must also be located in or willing to relocate to one of the following states: New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, Vermont, or Massachusetts, prior to hire. This position is fully onsite and does not allow telecommuting.HRI participates in the E-Verify Program. At HRI, we are on a mission to transform the health and well-being of the people of New York State through innovative partnerships and cutting-edge public health initiatives. As a dynamic non-profit organization, HRI plays a crucial role in advancing the strategic goals of the New York State Department of Health (DOH), Roswell Park Comprehensive Cancer Center (RPCCC), and other health-related entities. jobs.title: Development & Communications Intern at LIFT Inc
jobs.description: Employer: LIFT Inc Expires: 09/17/2026 POSITION: Development & Communications Intern LOCATION: National REPORTS TO: Director, Individual GivingSUPERVISES: N/AFLSA STATUS: NonexemptHOURLY RATE: $22TRAVEL, TIME COMMITMENT & Duration:Local In-Person External Meetings: 0%20-25 hours per month through December 31, 2026 with the possibility of extensionABOUT OUR ORGANIZATION LIFT is on a mission to break the cycle of poverty by investing in parents. Through direct work with families, engaging technical assistance partnerships, and by advocating for policies that drive systemic change, we’re fighting poverty by lifting two generations at once. Our team culture is rooted in deep respect for the parents we partner with and for each other. We’re looking for dedicated team members who share our vision that, 25 years from now, LIFT is no longer needed because we have helped build a social service system grounded in Hope, Money, and Love, where all families can thrive. We’re guided by mission- and strategy-aligned leadership grounded in kindness, curiosity, relationships, and a commitment to equity. Explore our benefits and what it’s like to work at LIFT below –or download our Benefits & Culture Overview to learn more.*LIFT operates sites in Chicago, Los Angeles, DC, and New York. This position may be done remotely from any state where LIFT currently operates.POSITION OVERVIEW This is a part-time internship requiring approximately 20 hours per month through December 31, 2026, with the possibility of extension. This role will report to the Director, Individual Giving, and will work closely with the Communications Manager. This part-time Development & Communications intern will support LIFT’s fundraising-focused communications efforts and external-facing communications. The internship is writing-driven, with responsibility for developing donor-facing communications, social media, and organizational content, creating compelling stories and content that engage supporters, strengthen relationships, advance fundraising goals, and broaden LIFT's reach and visibility.AS THE DEVELOPMENT & COMMUNICATION INTERN YOU WILL… DevelopmentDraft and edit donor-facing communications and development content that engage supporters, communicate impact, and strengthen relationships with donors and partners. Create and refine templates and adaptable content that can be used across multiple cities, ensuring consistency while tailoring messaging for local contexts.Support the development and execution of fundraising-focused communications strategies that effectively engage and retain donors.Develop clear, concise, and compelling written content that reflects both local impact and a broader national perspective.Collaborate with internal stakeholders to gather input and ensure alignment on messaging, while working independently.Proofread and edit content with a high level of attention to detail, ensuring accuracy, clarity, and consistency in tone and branding across materials.Explore opportunities to enhance communication through visual storytelling, including basic graphic design and video content to support fundraising efforts.Support broader development and communications activities, including event preparation, coordination, and administrative support as neededCommunicationsManage LIFT's social media presence day-to-day — writing and building posts, maintaining a consistent content calendar, and adapting content across platforms.Support the writing and editing of external content including the monthly newsletter, blog posts, and the annual report.Copy edit across external materials, serving as a reliable second pair of eyes on accuracy, consistency, tone, and brand.Track relevant news, research, and field conversations to surface content opportunities.OUR IDEAL CANDIDATE Strong writing and editing skills, with the ability to produce clear, concise, and compelling content for a range of audiences, including donors, partners, and social media audiences.Experience or interest in development and fundraising communications, donor engagement, and mission-driven storytelling.Fluency with social media as a communications tool. Comfortable writing copy and creating content for LinkedIn, Instagram, X, and Facebook, and maintaining a content calendar.Ability to work independently in a remote, flexible environment.High attention to detail, including proofreading for accuracy, consistency, and grammatical correctness.Self-motivated with a willingness to learn and grow skills in areas such as fundraising strategy, graphic design, and multimedia content (e.g., video).Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to contribute to longer-term projects by managing timelines, tracking tasks, and meeting deadlines.LIFT’S COMPETENCIESAll LIFT employees embrace and demonstrate our organization-wide core competencies:Communication: You share information with relevant parties in a clear and timely manner; effectively engage with and present to others; and write and verbally communicate in a manner that conveys understanding of relevant information and issues.Accountability: You take responsibility for the quality and timeliness of work and achieve results with appropriate levels of oversight. You receive feedback in a constructive manner.Inclusiveness: You help create a work environment that appreciates diversity and encourages equity by treating others with respect, listening to, and demonstrating appreciation for others’ perspectives, and using culturally sensitive language.Teamwork: You work effectively with others throughout the organization and promote cooperation and commitment within your team to achieve goals and deliverables.Results-orientation: You focus on results and desired outcomes, keeping team and organizational goals in mind. You use sound planning to achieve goals and get the job done.Problem-solving: You take the initiative to solve problems. You exhibit resourcefulness, innovation, and adaptability to new situations.Don’t think you have everything for this role but are still interested? Please don’t hesitate to apply. We’d love to hear from you! LIFT is an equal opportunity employer and believes that diversity in all dimensions of the organization supports and bolsters the innovative thinking essential to its success and is committed to providing equal employment opportunity to all qualified applicants. LIFT’s goal is for our people to reflect the communities in which we live and serve and to ensure representation of people of color, those who identify as women, veterans, and individuals with disabilities in our organization. WHAT WE OFFER Hourly rate: $22/hour. LIFT’s compensation philosophy is to pay competitively for our non-profit sector and ensure equity across the organization. The compensation range we offer represents a good faith estimate of what we may pay for the position at the time of posting. To ensure we meet our equity and inclusion standards, where a candidate is placed in the range will be assessed based on the market for the position, their qualifications, internal equity, and budget. We will discuss where you are likely to fall within the posted range during the recruitment process, and LIFT will present our best salary offer first.

jobs.title: Next Gen Organizing Intern at Bread for the World
jobs.description: Employer: Bread for the World Expires: 09/17/2026 Bread for the World is a Christian advocacy organization urging U.S. decision makers to do all they can to pursue a world without hunger. Our mission is to educate and equip people to advocate for policies and programs that can help end hunger in the U.S. and around the world. The Karen Sue Smith and Rose DiMartino Internship Program enables you to contribute your efforts to this mission while benefiting from opportunities for supervised learning, personal development, and gain work experience. DEPARTMENT: Organizing and Faith Engagement (ORG/FE) REPORTS TO: Next Gen Strategist SEMESTER: Fall (Sept. - Dec. 2026)SCHEDULE: Part Time: 15 hours per week APPLY BY: Sept. 4th, 2026PRIMARY PURPOSE: The next gen organizing intern will help build and mobilize a nationwide (and local) network of students through outreach and recruitment, supporting leadership development programs, coordinating events, and helping students take action on federal and state policy priorities. In general, the main projects for the next gen organizing intern include: Support national and local organizing efforts by recruiting and engaging students and young adults in advocacy campaigns and events.Research and build relationships with student groups, faculty, chaplains, and community partners to grow Bread for the World's NextGen network.Help plan and coordinate campus events, such as film screenings, discussions, and advocacy activities.Connect students to trainings and leadership opportunities and support the development of Student Leadership Teams on campusWork on additional projects as requested.SKILLS/KNOWLEDGE REQUIRED:Passion for social justice, advocacy, and ending hunger and poverty.Strong interpersonal and communication skills. Interest in organizing, leadership development, or public policy.Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a remote environment.Experience with or willingness to learn outreach, event planning, and social media engagement.Current college student or recent graduate preferred.WORK ENVIRONMENT ISSUES:This internship can be based in Washington, DC or remote in PA.Bread is a hybrid organization. CULTURAL EXPRESSIONS:Bread is committed to advancing racial equity externally and internally, all staff members play a vital role. In the course of our work, each staff person should work to apply a racial equity lens to their work and practices; and participate in racial equity on-going training. Bread is also committed to being an equal opportunity employer.OUR VALUES:We value our faith. Our faith in Christ compels us to love our neighbors near and far and is the foundation for our hope, story, mission, and values.We value human flourishing. We believe that every human being, created in the image of God, has inherent dignity that affords an opportunity to thrive in relationship with God, self, neighbor, and the environment; and to access enough nutritious food for good health.We value justice. We seek to establish effective systems, structures, and policies that affirm equality and advance equity among all human beings to alleviate hunger and poverty.We value courage and prophetic voice. In a spirit of wisdom and love, we will be bold in articulating and pursuing our vision of a world without hunger.We value nonpartisanship. We believe that effective and sustainable public policies are made when, in good faith, we employ a civil and bipartisan approach to develop and implement laws and programs to achieve our mission.We value collaboration. We believe in working alongside and building community with a diversity of churches, interfaith communities, institutions, and individuals, including people experiencing hunger, to achieve our mission.We value impact. We strive for excellence in our work and hold ourselves and our nation’s leaders accountable in the pursuit of public policies that render measurable results and meaningful change for people everywhere affected by hunger.DISCLAIMER:Background and reference checks will be conducted on all final candidates. The information in this job description indicates the general nature and level of work expected of employees in this classification. It is not designed to contain, nor to be interpreted as, a comprehensive inventory of all duties, responsibilities, qualifications, and objectives required of employees assigned to this job.

jobs.description: Employer: Scalp Trade Expires: 09/17/2026 We are seeking a driven and intellectually curious C++ Software Developer Intern to join our dynamic trading firm. This is an exceptional opportunity to gain hands-on experience building high-performance trading systems while contributing meaningfully to our operations. You will work closely with experienced engineers in a mentorship-rich environment, learning cutting-edge low-latency systems design, trading infrastructure, and modern C++ development practices. This internship is designed to accelerate your growth as a software engineer while you help develop tools and strategies that directly impact our trading operations. If you thrive on learning, enjoy solving complex technical problems, and want to understand how financial technology works at scale, this is the role for you. Key Responsibilities & Learning Objectives Develop and Optimize Components: Under mentor guidance, design and implement features for automated trading systems, with emphasis on understanding the 'why' behind architectural decisions in high-performance environments.Collaborative Development: Contribute to core trading platform enhancements alongside senior engineers, learning best practices for low-latency, distributed systems.Code Quality & Design: Learn and apply SOLID principles, modern C++ patterns, and system design concepts through hands-on code reviews and pair programming sessions.Performance Analysis: Participate in profiling and optimizing trading system components; understand tuning techniques for real-time operations.Documentation & Knowledge Sharing: Document code, design decisions, and lessons learned to build your technical communication skills.Problem-Solving: Work on well-scoped technical challenges that build your analytical and debugging skills in a production environment. Required Skills & QualificationsStrong Foundation in C++: Solid grasp of C++ fundamentals (STL, memory management, move semantics, templates). Production experience not required; demonstrated projects or coursework show readiness.Core CS Fundamentals: Comfortable with data structures, algorithms, and basic systems concepts (threading, process synchronization).Quick Learner: Able to rapidly pick up new tools, libraries, and frameworks with minimal guidance.Linux Familiarity: Comfortable working in Linux environments; shell scripting and command-line tools are a plus.Collaborative Mindset: Excellent communication skills; eager to learn from mentors and ask clarifying questions. Preferred Skills Multi-threading Experience: Practical familiarity with concurrent programming, thread safety, and synchronization primitives.Network Programming: Exposure to socket programming, TCP/IP, or distributed system basics.Additional Languages: Proficiency in Python, C#, or other systems languages broadens your perspective.Financial Markets Interest: Curiosity about trading, equities, options, or how financial markets work—we teach the rest.Database Exposure: Familiarity with SQL or understanding of how databases store and retrieve data at scale.Version Control & Tooling: Experience with Git, debugging tools (gdb, valgrind), or profilers (perf, flamegraph). Personal Attributes Intellectual Curiosity: Genuine interest in understanding how systems work, from code to infrastructure to business outcomes.Growth Mindset: Embrace challenges and feedback as opportunities to learn. We expect you to grow significantly over the internship.Ownership & Initiative: Proactive in seeking learning opportunities and taking on well-scoped responsibilities with minimal oversight.Adaptability: Comfortable with ambiguity and rapid changes; thriving in a fast-paced, high-performance environment.Collaborative Problem-Solving: Strong analytical skills with a preference for brainstorming and learning from teammates.Passion for Technology: Excitement about staying current with modern C++ and high-performance systems. What You'll GainHands-On Production Experience: Work in a real, production trading environment—not a sandbox. Your code runs strategies that generate revenue.Mentorship from Experts: Learn directly from senior engineers with deep expertise in low-latency systems, C++, and financial technology.Comprehensive Technical Knowledge: Understand high-performance systems design, from kernel tuning to network stack optimization.Career Acceleration: Build a portfolio of impactful projects and establish relationships with leaders in fintech.Potential for Conversion: Strong performers are considered for full-time roles upon graduation or at the conclusion of the internship. Compensation: This internship is paid at $7,000 per month for the program.

jobs.feedName: David Nazarian College of Business & Economics
jobs.title: Grant Writer Intern at Social Responsibility Through Me
jobs.description: Employer: Social Responsibility Through Me Expires: 09/18/2026 SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY THROUGH MEsrtme.org | Camden, NJ | info@srtmworks.orgPOSITION OPENSeptember 2026Grant Writer InternPaid Internship | Part-Time, Flexible | Remote-Friendly | September 2026 – May 2027 Position at a GlanceOrganizationSocial Responsibility Through Me (SRTM)Position TitleGrant Writer InternInternship PeriodSeptember 2026 – May 2027 (9 months)Hours Per Week15 hours/week — flexible scheduleLocationRemote work available; occasional in-person in Camden, NJ preferredStipend$3,000 for the full internship period (September–May)Performance Bonus$500 bonus available upon achievement of grant goalEligibilityCurrently enrolled college students (sophomore, junior, or senior preferred)Reports ToCEO / Development Director, Shaneka M. Boucher About Social Responsibility Through MeSocial Responsibility Through Me (SRTM) is a Camden, New Jersey nonprofit organization founded in 2010 with a mission to engage, employ, and empower youth and adults in underserved communities. Through afterschool enrichment programs, workforce development, and community partnerships, SRTM creates pathways to economic mobility for the families we serve. Our programs currently support over 700 youth and adults. iWe operate multiple afterschool sites across Camden City and County, and are in an active growth phase with a $1.6 million operating budget and a $315,000 fundraising goal for 2026–2027. This internship is a genuine opportunity to contribute to work that directly changes lives — and to build real, résumé-ready grant writing experience in the process. The OpportunitySRTM is seeking a motivated, detail-oriented college student to join our development team as a Grant Writer Intern for the 2026–2027 academic year. This is not a filing or data-entry internship. You will be doing real grant writing — researching funders, drafting narrative proposals, compiling application materials, and submitting grants on behalf of an organization whose work you will come to know deeply. By the end of this internship, you will have submitted a minimum of 5 grant applications to real funders, built a portfolio of professional writing samples, developed a working knowledge of the NJ philanthropic landscape, and gained hands-on experience in nonprofit development that most students don't access until their first professional job. Compensation & Bonus Structure BASE STIPEND$3,000Paid over the full internship period (September 2026 – May 2027). Disbursed in monthly installments of approximately $333/month.PERFORMANCE BONUS$500Awarded at the end of the internship period if the intern successfully submits all 5 assigned grant applications by their deadlines, with all required components complete and meeting SRTM's quality standard. Total PotentialA Grant Writer Intern who meets all goals can earn $3,500 total over the 9-month internship — $3,000 base stipend + $500 performance bonus. Payment terms: the base stipend will be issued as 1099 compensation. Interns are responsible for their own taxes. SRTM will issue the $500 bonus upon verification that all 5 applications were submitted on time and meet quality standards as determined by the CEO. Core ResponsibilitiesThe Grant Writer Intern is responsible for the following activities across the internship period: GRANT RESEARCH & CALENDAR MANAGEMENTResearch and identify grant opportunities aligned with SRTM's mission in youth development, workforce development, afterschool programming, and economic mobility.Verify funder eligibility requirements — geographic focus, organizational eligibility, program alignment, and award range — before recommending any grant for pursuit.Maintain SRTM's Grant Calendar tab: update deadlines, application status, assigned amounts, and notes for all grants in the pipeline.Provide the CEO with a bi-weekly pipeline update identifying grants due in the next 60 days and any action items requiring CEO input. GRANT WRITING & APPLICATION PREPARATIONDraft full grant narratives for a minimum of 5 grant applications across the internship period, working from SRTM's program data, impact reports, and the Fundraising SOP framework.Write clearly and compellingly for nonprofit funders — leading with outcomes and data, not activities; using Camden-specific community need data to contextualize SRTM's work.Compile all required application attachments: IRS determination letter, 990, board list, audited financials, organizational budget, and program one-pagers — from SRTM's Grant Ready Folder.Ensure all applications are submitted a minimum of 72 hours before the funder's deadline. No exceptions.Submit all applications through the funder's required portal or method, save confirmation receipts, and update the Grant Tracker the same day as submission. GRANT TRACKING & REPORTING SUPPORTUpdate SRTM's Grant Tracker within 24 hours of any grant activity — application submitted, funder contact made, award or decline received.Support the Development Director in preparing interim and final grant reports for active grants as assigned.Help compile program outcome data from SRTM's five dashboard trackers (Attendance, Behavior, Homework, Voucher, Manager) for use in grant applications and reports.Assist with writing thank-you letters and acknowledgments to funders upon grant awards. LEARNING & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENTParticipate in weekly check-in meetings with the CEO/Development Director (30 minutes, remote or in-person).Attend at least one NJ nonprofit or funder information session during the internship period (virtual attendance acceptable).Review and apply SRTM's Fundraising Standard Operating Procedures as the guide for all development activities.Provide written feedback at the midpoint and end of the internship on the experience, challenges, and suggestions for improvement. The 5-Grant Goal — What Success Looks LikeThe intern is responsible for submitting 5 complete, quality grant applications between September 2026 and May 2027. These will be selected collaboratively with the CEO from SRTM's Grant Calendar based on the intern's start date, funder deadlines, and available program data. Below is a sample of what the 5-grant portfolio might look like: #Funder (Sample)Ask AmountTarget DeadlineCategory1Turrell Fund (NJ)$15,000–$25,000Sept/Oct 2026Youth Development / Afterschool2Campbell Soup Foundation$10,000–$20,000Jan 2027Education / Community (Camden)3Claneil Foundation$5,000–$15,000Feb 2027General Operating / Youth4TD Charitable Foundation$10,000–$20,000Rolling 2027Education / Workforce5NJ DOE After3 or similar$20,000–$50,000Spring 2027Afterschool / Academic Support Final grant selections will be confirmed during the intern's first week based on actual funder deadlines, current Grant Calendar status, and SRTM's program data availability. The intern will not be expected to submit grants for which SRTM does not have the necessary supporting documentation. What We Are Looking For Required QualificationsCurrently enrolled as a college sophomore, junior, or senior (or recent graduate within 6 months of graduation)Strong written communication skills — ability to write clearly, concisely, and compellingly for a professional audienceDetail-oriented and highly organized — grant writing is unforgiving of errors and missed deadlinesSelf-directed and able to work independently with minimal supervision in a remote environmentComfortable with Google Workspace or Microsoft Office (Docs/Word, Sheets/Excel)Genuine interest in nonprofit work, social justice, youth development, or community economic developmentPreferred QualificationsCoursework or experience in nonprofit management, public policy, social work, communications, English, education, or a related fieldPrevious writing experience — journalism, academic research, persuasive writing, communications internship, or similarFamiliarity with grant writing or fundraising concepts (even from a class or volunteer experience)Knowledge of Camden, NJ or experience working in under-resourced communitiesAbility to visit SRTM's Camden site at least once during the internship period What You Will GainThis internship is designed to give you real professional experience — not make-work tasks. Here is what you will leave with: Portfolio of Real Work5 submitted grant applications to real funders — professional writing samples you can use in job applications and interviews immediately.Sector KnowledgeA working understanding of the NJ philanthropic landscape, including how community foundations, corporate foundations, and government funders make decisions.Nonprofit Operations ExperienceExposure to a real nonprofit's development systems, program data, and funding strategy — the behind-the-scenes work most students don't see until their first job.Professional MentorshipWeekly direct access to SRTM's CEO, who has 15+ years of experience in nonprofit leadership and community development in South Jersey.Letters of RecommendationStrong performers will receive a detailed, personalized letter of recommendation from the CEO upon completion of the internship.Professional NetworkConnections to SRTM's partner organizations, employer partners, and NJ nonprofit community — a network that takes most people years to build.Schedule, Location & Logistics Hours15 hours per week. The intern and supervisor will agree on a schedule during the first week. Hours are flexible and can be arranged around class schedules.Remote WorkThe majority of work can be completed remotely. Interns are expected to attend weekly virtual check-in meetings and may be asked to visit SRTM's Camden office occasionally for orientation, events, or collaborative sessions.Internship PeriodSeptember 2026 – May 2027. The intern is expected to complete the full internship period to receive the full stipend. Interns who leave before May 2027 will receive a prorated stipend based on months completed. The $500 bonus requires full completion.ToolsSRTM uses Google Workspace (Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Drive). All grant tracking, research, and writing will be conducted in shared Google documents. A personal laptop or computer with internet access is required.Academic CreditSRTM is happy to support academic internship credit requirements. The CEO will complete any required supervisor evaluations or forms needed by your institution. How to ApplySRTM welcomes applications from college students of all backgrounds, especially those with personal connections to Camden or communities like it. You do not need prior grant writing experience to apply — you need strong writing skills, curiosity, and the drive to do the work. #SubmitDetails1RésuméCurrent résumé — one page preferred. Include all relevant coursework, writing experience, volunteer work, or extracurriculars.2Writing SampleOne writing sample of your choice — ideally something persuasive, research-based, or analytical. Academic papers are fine. If you have any nonprofit or grant writing samples, include those.3Short Cover LetterNo more than one page. Tell us: why SRTM's mission connects with you, what writing experience you bring (any kind), and what you hope to learn from this internship. Be specific — generic cover letters are immediately apparent.4OptionalIf you have completed any grant writing courses, workshops, or have access to a sample grant application you have written, include it as a bonus attachment. Send Applications ToNicquera Allen: msnallen@srtme.orgApplication DeadlineRolling — applications reviewed as received. Priority consideration given to applications submitted by August 15, 2026. Internship begins September 2026.Questions?Reach out to Ms. Nicquera Allen directly at msnallen@srtme.org or 856-952-2574. SRTM is a small team and we respond to every inquiry personally. Equal Opportunity StatementSocial Responsibility Through Me is an equal opportunity organization. We actively welcome applications from students of color, first-generation college students, students from Camden and South Jersey, students with disabilities, and students who bring lived experience in the communities we serve. We believe the best grant writers for SRTM are those who understand our community from the inside.SRTM does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.description: Employer: Mars, Inc. Expires: 09/19/2026 At Mars, we work together to build a better world for people, pets, and the planet. From being a socially responsible business, to investing in our Associates, we're always looking at how we can make tomorrow brighter. As an Associate, you are empowered with the freedom and tools to be yourself, to forge your own path, to build relationships across our global community, to discover the right opportunities for you to grow – all with ample support. Here, you have our ongoing commitment to your growth and development as you work across our world-famous brands. Start your journey at Mars today! Mars KIND Finance Internship Experience As a KIND Finance Intern, you will gain exposure to the following areas: Help our finance teams drive our digital agenda by unlocking analytics capabilities, processes and helping to mold the usage and adoption of next generation applications and technologies Collaborate with various stakeholders to drive value through tangible, project-based assignments (vary depending on business need) with visibility to senior leadership within the organization Build capability in sought after skills including but not limited to data storytelling, analysis, process optimization, senior leader communication, project ownership and stakeholder alignment A competitive experience with the potential to join full-time within the MARS Finance Leadership Experience (MFLE) program post-graduation after a successful internship and candidate evaluation. What we’re looking for: We are looking for agile students who have a drive for results, a desire to learn, and who can quickly build relationships We are looking for students who are passionate about the consumer products industry and are majoring in Finance, Accounting, or related business fields Eligible candidates will intern the summer prior to their final graduation date (typically rising seniors) Willingness to relocate to the site of the role Open to students legally authorized to work in the U.S., without the need for current or future work sponsorship Employment is contingent upon successful completion of drug & background screening Eligible candidates will be responsible for personal transportation to and from work site during duration of the internship program. What can you expect from Mars? The Mars Internship Experience is a 10-week summer program providing excellent depth of experience with real business problems and opportunities. Exciting professional and social engagement activities throughout the experience that provide opportunities to network with your intern peers all the way up to senior leaders. Best-in-class training and development from Day 1, including a formal mentor, access to our in-house Mars University, and more. Ongoing coaching and mentorship to help you succeed and get the most out of your experience. Some pretty sweet perks including competitive salary & benefits package, fun freebies, and pet-friendly offices. About Mars, Incorporated For more than a century, Mars, Incorporated has been driven by the belief that the world we want tomorrow starts with how we do business today. This idea is at the center of who we have always been as a global, family-owned business. Today, Mars is transforming, innovating, and evolving in ways that affirm our commitment to making a positive impact on the world around us. Across our diverse and expanding portfolio of Snacking, Food, and Petcare products and services, we employ over 140,000 dedicated Associates who are all moving in the same direction: forward. As a $65 billion family-owned business, we produce some of the world’s best-loved brands including ROYAL CANIN®, PEDIGREE®, WHISKAS®, CESAR®, M&M’S®, SNICKERS®, Pringles®, Cheez-It®, and BEN’S ORIGINAL™. and take care of half of the world’s pets through our nutrition, health and services businesses, including AniCura, Banfield Pet Hospitals™, BluePearl®, Linnaeus, and VCA™. We know we can only be truly successful if our partners and the communities in which we operate prosper as well. The Mars Five Principles – Quality, Responsibility, Mutuality, Efficiency and Freedom – inspire our Associates to take action every day to help create a world tomorrow in which the planet, its people and pets can thrive. The Mars Compass, inspired by the Economics of Mutuality, is used to measure the company’s progress in service of its purpose; The world we want tomorrow starts with how we do business today. For more information about Mars, please visit mars.com. Join us on Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, Instagram and YouTube.

jobs.description: Employer: Polaris Inc. Expires: 09/19/2026 Internship Program Overview The Polaris Engineering Internship is a tailored 12-week paid summer internship designed for emerging juniors, and seniors who are interested in pursuing a career in a leading global powersports industry. This program is for future leaders who seek a culture built on innovation, passion, and collaboration. As an Engineering Intern, you will be given impactful, project-based assignments that allow you to have exposure to multiple facets of engineering so you will experience both larger ongoing projects as well as shorter-scale projects throughout the summer that align with our business objectives. You will be placed into a specific team based on interest and business needs. These teams could include, but are not limited to: Design Engineering Project Engineering Systems Engineering Test or Development Engineering Potential Placement Locations Could Include: Roseau, MN; Wyoming, MN; Huntsville, AL; or San Angelo, TX, Novi, MI As a Polaris intern it is important that you embrace the adventure and remain open to any placement opportunity. By being adaptable, you will gain diverse experiences and develop a broader skill set, which are essential for your professional development and success within Polaris. Our internship program is crafted to build the foundational skills and experiences essential for your career success. Upon completing the internship, those who demonstrate exceptional performance and a strong passion for learning may be offered a returning internship or a position in our rotational leadership development program. In addition to meaningful project work, you will participate in intentional programming and professional development offerings such as: Mentorship: you are paired with one of our DP associates for mentor support throughout your 12-weeks. Programming Hours: weekly functional and centralized learning sessions to broaden your knowledge base, both within and beyond your program. Networking: intentional time with peers and leaders at Polaris to build your professional network. Intern Innovation Challenge: internal case study designed to promote cross functional development where you and your team will present creative and practical solutions to a real ‘Polaris’ problem to our executive leadership. Early Talent Summit Week: participate in our 3-day event in our Wyoming, MN office. This immersive experience brings together all US interns and DPs for professional development, structured networking, a DP graduation event, inspiring executive speakers, and a thrilling team ride on some of your favorite Polaris vehicles. Community Engagement: opportunity to get involved in your local community. Final Presentations: present to our senior level leaders to showcase your career aspirations and recap your internship experience. The Selection Process: Applications are open from August -November each year. Applications will be reviewed and shortlisted candidates will typically be contacted for an initial phone screen by the end of November. Candidates selected to move forward will be invited to participate in a virtual panel interview with an identified HR business partner and functional leader. Successful candidates would move forward to an offer. You will partner with the Early Talent team in January to complete a survey that provides a deeper look at your specific interests, strengths & career goals. All specific internship assignments are communicated in February, after aligning based on your specific interests and business demand. Intern Relocation Assistance: Polaris offers a relocation program for interns who qualify through our mobility vendor. To qualify for these services, your home address must be 35 miles or more from the office where you will be working. Benefits include a lump sum (grossed up to offset tax liability), access to a relocation counselor to explain the resources available to you and aid in securing short-term housing available to you. Your responsibilities will include daily transportation to and from the office. Required Qualifications: Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master's degree in Engineering (e.g. mechanical, electrical, computer, software, or systems engineering) with an intended graduation date between August 2027-May 2029. Minimum overall GPA of 3.0 Able to complete full 12-week internship working 40 hours per week within the dates: May 17th – August 6th, 2027. June 1st – August 20th, 2027. Willing and able to relocate. Must be a U.S. person (U.S. citizen, U.S. national, lawful permanent resident, asylee, or refugee) and not require sponsorship for employment now or in the future. Must have reliable transportation for daily commuting to and from the office. Previous experience with Microsoft Office software tools (Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Teams, and Word). Preferred Qualifications: Demonstrated strengths in analysis, creative problem-solving, communication, interpersonal relationships, self-motivation, and leadership. Strong interest in long-term career development and participation in leadership development programs. Previous leadership experience in work, organizations, or classroom. Completion of at least two years of university coursework Previous Internship/Co-op experience Previous experience using CAD or equivalent software (Creo highly desired) Hands-on engineering experience through prior internship or clubs (ex. SAE, Clean Snow) This is more than an internship - It's the beginning of your career with Polaris. We hope you're ready for the ultimate adventure!

jobs.description: Employer: LifeWorks Expires: 09/19/2026 Fundraising & Events Intern InternshipLocation: Austin, TX |Part-time (10-17 hours/week) ***Please note this role is for currently enrolled students who will be receiving class credit for the internship. Compensation for this position is an end-of-semester stipend (one-time payment) in the amount of $825.00.*** Solving Youth Homelessness - TogetherAt LifeWorks, our mission is to solve youth homelessness through housing, mental health, education, and workforce programs. Our team walks alongside youth on their journeys toward stability and independence, always centering their voices and strengths. This internship provides hands-on experience supporting fundraising operations, donor engagement, revenue strategy, and special events. The intern will play an integral role in maintaining high-quality donor data, supporting prospect research, coordinating fundraising events, and improving internal processes that help advance LifeWorks' mission. This is an ideal opportunity for a detail-oriented, organized, and analytical student interested in nonprofit fundraising, operations, business intelligence, event management, or project coordination.Key ResponsibilitiesRevenue Operations Support documentation of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), workflows, and best practices for CRM usage, data governance, activity tracking, and moves management.Prospect Research & Fundraising SupportConduct donor and prospect research, including wealth screening and identification of potential major gift prospects.Prepare research summaries and portfolio recommendations for frontline fundraisers.Assist with donor segmentation, reporting, and fundraising analytics to support strategic decision-making.Event Planning & Donor EngagementSupport planning and execution of Lunch for LifeWorks, the organization's signature annual fundraising event, along with other donor cultivation events throughout the semester.Assist with guest communications, RSVP tracking, and event registration management.Coordinate logistical communication with vendors, venues, caterers, and A/V partners.Help manage sponsor benefit fulfillment, ensuring all recognition and deliverables are completed accurately and on schedule.Prepare day-of-event materials including seating charts, run-of-show documents, volunteer assignments, name badges, and event packets.Participate in event planning meetings by preparing agendas, documenting action items, and tracking project progress.Administrative & Project CoordinationBuild and maintain project tracking systems and timelines.Support cross-functional collaboration across the Development team.Assist with special projects and operational initiatives as assigned. What You'll GainThroughout this internship, you'll gain valuable experience in:Nonprofit fundraising operations and development strategyCRM administration and database managementBusiness intelligence, reporting, and dashboard developmentProspect research and donor pipeline managementEvent planning and execution for large-scale fundraising eventsVendor and sponsor relationship managementProject management and process improvementData analysis using Excel, including Pivot Tables, lookups, segmentation, and reportingProfessional communication with donors, sponsors, and community partnersCross-functional collaboration within a nonprofit organizationWho We're Looking ForCurrent student in Nonprofit Management, Public Administration, Communications, Business, or related fields. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook). Familiarity with basic database queries. Ability to write persuasively and professionally with a keen eye for tone and detail. Someone who finds satisfaction in "clean" project boards and ensuring no detail falls through the cracks. Ability to handle sensitive donor and financial information with the utmost discretion.A genuine interest in solving youth homelessness and understanding the systems that drive community changes.

jobs.description: Employer: Air Force Civilian Service - Air Force Civilian Service Expires: 09/19/2026 PREMIER COLLEGE INTERN PROGRAM (PCIP)AFCS's full-time PCIP prepares college students for a number of promising career fields within AFCS, including Science and Engineering, Cybersecurity, IT, Acquisition, and other mission-critical specialty positions. jobs.description: Employer: Community for Sustainable Energy Expires: 09/19/2026 Join a team working in common cause to create a sustainable energy future!Community for Sustainable Energy is a Fort Collins based grassroots organization dedicated to the practice of democracy in pursuit of a more sustainable society.We are hiring for entry level internships with our campaign staff to:Raise public awareness of Colorado energy concernsReach 100% Renewable Electricity in Fort CollinsPrevent the construction of new fossil fuel plants in Northern COGet public schools to go solarHold local officials accountable to their sustainability goalsWorking with CforSE is like an intensive/immersive 7 hour class. jobs.description: Employer: County of Orange - County of Orange Expires: 09/19/2026 Position Land Survey Paid Intern (Technical Intern)Deadline to ApplyPlease note the deadline for this recruitment is Wednesday, September 2, 2026, at 11:59 PM (PT). OC Public Works (OCPW) provides services on a regional basis to unincorporated areas, to cities, and to other County agencies and departments. The primary mission of the department is to protect and enrich the community through the sustainable delivery of projects and services. OC Public Works’ guiding principles are safety, integrity, quality, teamwork, and adaptability.OCPW is a unique County department comprised of ten (10) service areas: Administrative Services, Agricultural Commissioner/Sealer of Weights & Measures; OC Construction; OC Development Services; OC Environmental Resources; OC Facilities Design & Construction and CUF; OC Facilities Maintenance; OC Fleet Services; OC Infrastructure Programs; OC Operations & Maintenance.OC CONSTRUCTIONOC Construction provides project management and construction management services for projects on OC Public Works' Capital Improvement Program (CIP) and Maintenance Improvement Program (MIP) as well as OC Parks and other County department projects. OC Construction focuses on horizontal projects such as roads, bridges, bikeways, and flood control channels.For more information on OC Public Works click here.For more information on the County of Orange click here.THE OPPORTUNITYThe Land Survey Intern position provides students with valuable hands-on experience by working alongside licensed land surveyors and experienced professionals on a wide variety of public infrastructure projects throughout Orange County. Interns have the opportunity to apply classroom knowledge in a real-world setting while gaining exposure to both office and field surveying practices. Land Survey Interns will assist survey staff with a variety of office and field assignments.Land Survey Interns will assist survey staff with a variety of office and field assignments, including: Assisting with boundary, topographic, construction, hydrographic, and control surveys. Collecting field measurements using GNSS, total stations, digital levels, terrestrial laser scanners, and UAV technologies. Processing field data and assisting with drafting, mapping, and preparation of survey deliverables using CAD and survey software. Assisting with research of deeds, maps, survey records, right-of-way documents, and other legal records. Organizing project files, field notes, and digital records. Performing other related technical duties that support the Survey-Field Services unit while developing practical knowledge of professional land surveying practices. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONSThis recruitment is open to applicants who are currently enrolled in or have graduated within the last six (6) months from an accredited college or university pursuing a degree or certificate in Land Surveying, Geomatics, Civil Engineering, or a closely related field. Completion of introductory coursework in mathematics, surveying, engineering, or mapping is desirable. Ability to perform basic mathematical calculations and pay close attention to detail. SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONSThe ideal candidate for this Internship will have basic computer skills, including proficiency with Microsoft Office applications. Interest in learning modern land surveying principles, field procedures, and office workflows; surveying equipment, including GNSS/GPS receivers, total stations, digital levels, laser scanners, and other survey technologies; and survey software, including AutoCAD Civil 3D, Trimble Business Center (TBC), GIS applications, or similar programs. Ability to communicate effectively, follow written and verbal instructions, and work effectively both independently and as part of a team.TIME COMMITMENTThis is an in-person internship. Interns may work 26-30 hours per week for 1 year (part-time) not to exceed 1,040 hours. Hours must be scheduled during normal business hours (Monday - Thursday between 6:00am and 3:30pm & Friday between 6:00am and 2:30pm).BENEFITS AVAILABLE TO THE INTERNInterns are offered an excellent opportunity to:Provides students with valuable hands-on experience working alongside licensed land surveyors and experienced professionals.Offers exposure to a wide variety of public infrastructure projects throughout Orange County.Allows interns to apply classroom knowledge in a real-world setting.Provides exposure to both office and field surveying practices.Helps students develop skills and knowledge relevant to entry-level surveying positions.Provides OC Public Works with a larger candidate pool for the entry-level Surveyor I position.Explore a career in local government.Mentorship from management staff.Network with professionals.Apply knowledge through real life application and best practices in field.APPLICATION PROCEDUREApplicants must attach a cover letter, resume, and unofficial transcripts to their application. The cover letter is an opportunity for students to describe career and academic goals, to elaborate upon personal and academic accomplishments, and to identify what type of internship experience they are seeking. Learn more about what to include in a cover letter HERE.Applications that do not include a cover letter, resume, and unofficial transcripts will not be considered.REQUIRED BACKGROUND SCREENING/REFERENCE CHECKPrior to placement, applicants may be asked to submit contact information for reference checks, and a background screening will be conducted that requires a state issued driver's license or ID card and a U.S. Social Security number.

jobs.description: Employer: WPAFB Program Manager Trainee Program Expires: 09/20/2026 About WPAFB Program Manager Trainee ProgramLooking for Civilian Program Managers to lead the Air Force into the 21st centuryOne of six centers under Air Force Materiel Command, the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center is the single center responsible for total life cycle management of Air Force weapon systems.The AFLCMC Mission: "Acquire and Support War-Winning Capabilities"Our Motto: "AFLCMC...Providing the Warfighter's Edge"We are currently recruiting Sophomore or Junior students to come work for the U.S. Air Force at Wright-Patterson AFB as a Program Manager in the Premier College Intern Program for the summer of 2027. What is a Program Manager (PM)? What does a Program Manager do in the Air Force?An Acquisition Program Manager leads a team of multi-functional professionals in the acquisition and support of Air Force weapon systems: aircraft, weapons, training systems, IT and business systems at the Air Force Life Cycle Management Center (AFLCMC). As an Air Force program manager you will be responsible for managing and coordinating all aspects of an acquisition program to achieve the cost, schedule, performance and sustainment goals of your customers, the men and women who fly, operate, or maintain this country’s most advanced aircraft and systems. Your primary role will be that of the team leader. jobs.description: Employer: AppleOne Employment Services Expires: 09/20/2026 About ActOne GroupActOne Group Industries builds and deploys AI agents and automations that run real business workflows for enterprise clients. Our platform, Foundry, lets teams design, build, and ship AI applications and agents — and we work side-by-side with clients to get those solutions into production. We're a small, fast-moving team where the work you do reaches customers quickly. About the RoleThis is a Forward Deployment Engineer (FDE) internship — but you don't need a traditional engineering background. You need sharp business instincts, genuine curiosity about AI, and the drive to learn how to build.Forward Deployment Engineers sit at the intersection of client and product. You'll learn how to translate a client's business problems into working AI agents and applications, build them on Foundry using Claude Code, and help clients do the same. A big part of the summer is helping us design and build a client training program — alongside our AI Lead — that teaches customers how to build their own AI applications and agents from scratch.If you've been the person who picks up new tools fast, builds things on the side, and likes being in the room with customers, this is for you. Why This Is an Exciting OpportunityThe way work gets done is being rewritten right now, and Forward Deployment Engineers are the people doing the rewriting. You won't be watching the AI shift from the sidelines — you'll be on the front line of it, sitting with real businesses and turning "what if AI could do this?" into something that's actually running in production.This is a rare chance to get genuinely fluent in the tools and workflows that will define the next decade of work, while you're still early. You'll build real AI agents and applications, shape how clients learn to build their own, and develop a skill set very few people have yet: knowing how to take AI from a demo to deployed value. The people who learn this now — how to think with these tools, sell with them, and ship with them — are the ones who will be leading teams and companies in a few years. We're betting that's you. What You'll DoWork directly with clients to understand their workflows, goals, and where AI can create real valueLearn to build AI agents and applications on the Foundry platform using Claude CodeHelp design and build our client-facing training program alongside the AI Lead — the curriculum that teaches clients how to build and deploy their own AI solutionsSupport client onboarding and the hands-on deployment of solutionsGet deep, practical exposure to the leading AI tools — Claude, OpenAI, and the broader stack — and develop strong judgment about when and how to use eachDocument patterns, write clear guides, and turn what works into repeatable playbooks Who You AreStrong business fundamentals — you understand how companies actually operate and make decisionsHands-on AI exposure — you've used tools like Claude and OpenAI extensively, ideally building real things with them, not just experimentingA fast, self-directed learner — comfortable with ambiguity and figuring things out without a manualA clear communicator — you can hold your own in a client conversation and explain technical ideas in plain termsPrior startup or technology experience (required) — you've worked at a startup or tech company, founded something, or built and shipped your own product. You know what it's like to move fast in an environment without a playbook.Currently enrolled in a college or university program Bonus PointsA portfolio of AI projects you've built — apps, agents, automations, prompts, anythingFamiliarity with no-code/low-code tools or prompt engineeringExperience in a client-facing, sales, or consulting setting The DetailsLocation: Los Angeles, CA — hybrid (mix of in-person and remote)Duration: SemesterCompensation: Discussed during the interview processGrowth: Strong interns will be considered for a full-time offer after the summer

jobs.description: Employer: Inner Peak Expires: 09/21/2026 Marketing Intern: B2B Growth & Digital PresenceInner Peak builds mental health support for students, and we sell it to K-12 districts and universities. The team is small. There is no marketing function yet, and that's why we are hiring you: you'd be building it next to our VP of Sales & Marketing, who you'd report to directly.Worth saying up front, we don't have a playbook to hand you. We're still writing it. Some of what you try is going to flop. That's ok. We are paying you to learn together with us. The work:Build and run a monthly email campaign to actual prospects: superintendents, student services directors, deans of student affairsRun our LinkedIn page. What goes out, how often, who we engage with, how fast the following growsDo the same for Instagram and TikTok, which are earlier and messierSet up and manage paid campaigns on LinkedIn, Meta, and Google.
